label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. 91% of activation mass is at the last step (t=5, recalling original token 2) of L=3 sequences, where it fires on about 94% of such sequences. Its input there is the fed-back original token 1, i.e. prev2_tok is <DEL>. Weaker spillover: L=4 sequences at the second-to-last and last copy steps (t=6 and t=7, ~9% of mass, firing on only a few percent of L=4 sequences). Essentially silent for L>=5, in the original phase, and at the delimiter. Magnitude varies a little with the input token (o, r, w highest), and the top examples are all L=3 final steps. Low-quartile activations are mostly the L=4 cases.

issues: Store mismatch: you asked for features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but the autointerp tool can't load it. It only holds raw .pt files and a subsample manifest, with no sequences.pkl, so running profile on it fails with FileNotFoundError. So this verification, like the original one, ran on features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. The 1/5 subsample has to be converted into a store before the baseline can run on it.

I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.951, R 0.742, F1 0.833, mass recall 0.921. Quartile coverage of the predicate is 0.28/0.73/0.96/1.00, so the misses are concentrated in the low-activation tail, as claimed.

The factual claims check out. The unit never fires in the original phase or at the delimiter (t<L has 0 active steps). It fires on about 94% of L=3 sequences at t=5. L=4 spillover at t=6 and t=7 carries about 8.5% of the mass on dev. L>=5 is essentially silent: 29 active steps on dev, about 0.1% of the mass.

Minor omission: the unit is markedly weaker when the input at the L=3 final step is 'n'. Only 41% of those 92 test steps fire, and they account for a sizable share of the 128 false positives. This is a small magnitude effect, not a separate class.

I couldn't explain the L=4 spillover. I tried copy errors (correct==0 never occurs), repeated tokens, digit inputs, and prev_tok==orig(0); all have precision of 4% or less. It reads as low-magnitude leakage onto the nearby condition, not a coherent second meaning.
Excluding in_tok 'n' gives the same test F1 (0.8335 vs 0.833), so no better predicate is worth proposing.
